body.x: On a sprawling construction or shipbuilding site, nothing stays where the plan said it would, so tracking what is actually built is a daily guess. Reading the real site as live data, instead of scanning barcodes, is a different way to know.
LiOps Inc. was named a 2027 Honoree in Artificial Intelligence at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for LiOps Spatial MES, a live operating layer for industrial sites.

LiOps Spatial MES is a two-layer platform that turns ever-changing industrial sites into live, machine-readable operating data and puts robots to work on it. The sensing layer replaces the barcode: proprietary fixed-LiDAR scanning and GPU-accelerated deep learning make CAD registration hundreds of times faster than conventional ICP, automatically identifying every workpiece and measuring per-part assembly progress in real time, feeding actuals into existing ERP/MES with zero site preparation.

At the execution layer, autonomous robot welding crews operate on the same coordinates, performing unstructured welding with zero jigs, teaching or fixed trajectories and billed strictly by completed output, as heavy industry has bought labor for decades. Each layer stands alone, and both are already sold under paid contracts.
The platform applies wherever large structures are built, including shipbuilding, EPC, plant, steel fabrication and offshore energy.

The CES Innovation Awards program, an annual competition honoring outstanding design and engineering in consumer technology products, recognizes all recipients as Honorees at two levels. The Honoree level covers products that score above the scoring threshold in each category, while Best of Innovation goes to the highest-scoring Honorees. A panel of industry expert judges and global media scores each product on engineering and functionality, aesthetic and design, and what makes it unique and innovative.

AVING NEWS, a global media company with 21 years of experience covering CES, operates AVING CES Newsroom (avingces.news), a dedicated platform for delivering the latest innovations to global audiences. Publishing more than 1,000 articles and conducting hundreds of on-site video interviews annually, AVING NEWS has helped Korean startups gain international visibility and expand their global reach. At CES 2027, AVING NEWS will operate the AVING TECH TALK broadcast zone at the Venetian Expo (Hall A, Booth 50271), providing on-site coverage and interviews that spotlight Korean companies and their latest innovations.
* AVING NEWS uses AI-assisted tools in its editorial process.
